title: Bounded-above complexes resolved by a zero-preserving left resolution
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a preadditive category with a zero object and finite coproducts, and let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful and additive. Suppose $Q:A\to C$ is a functor preserving zero morphisms and $\pi:\iota Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ is a natural transformation with epimorphic components. On the full subcategory of integer cochain complexes whose terms vanish in all sufficiently large degrees, there are a functor $S$ to integer cochain complexes in $A$ and a natural transformation $a:S\Rightarrow\iota_-$, where $\iota_-$ is the inclusion, such that every $a_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every term of $S(L)$ is isomorphic to an object in the essential image of $\iota$, and every upper bound for $L$ is an upper bound for $S(L)$. This functor is defined on all maps in the bounded-above full subcategory, regardless of which upper-bound witnesses are chosen.
